newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda seeks buyers for its biggest bank.
newsitem.headline: Uganda seeks buyers for its biggest bank.

text.p: Uganda's government on Thursday invited investors to buy a 51-percent stake in the state-owned Uganda Commercial Bank (UCB), the largest bank in the country.
The finance ministry's privatisation unit invited potential investors to submit proposals by March 14 for a stake in the bank, which has 85 outlets and one-third the total deposits in the country.
"Short-listed prospective investors shall be provided the opportunity to carry out detailed due diligence on UCB before submitting a final and binding bid proposal," the unit said in a statement.
The core investor would be expected to take up to 51 percent in the bank while the government would retain 49 percent for sale either to Ugandan investors or at a later date.

Debtors have defaulted on UCB loans of 70 billion shillings. The government has promised to pump 70 billion shillings in bonds into UCB as recapitalisation before it is privatised. ($1=1035 Ugandan shillings)
